newsitem.title: UK: EU grain prices tick down on subdued demand.
newsitem.headline: EU grain prices tick down on subdued demand.

text.p: Sluggish export business has weighed on European grain prices this week with the exception of Germany which continues to ride on the back of eastern demand.
Grain prices eased across much of the European Union (EU) but maize bucked the trend on lack of spot availability.
In France, maize seized the spotlight as prompt prices rose sharply. Traders attributed the hike to rains which slowed combining of early crops, threatening to disrupt deliveries.
Spot Bordeaux maize was offered at 1,030 francs, up 10 francs on the week. Forward deliveries were unchanged.
Wheat and barley suffered from lack of exports after last week's EU tender which left most bids uncovered.
Exporters anxious to cover a great deal of a Saudi purchase of 1.4 million tonnes of feed barley and wheat to Egypt are expected to put pressure on the EU to grant more subsidies.
But the overall mood was bearish ahead of Thursday's tender.
Sellers in Germany however stuck to their guns despite a Ministry of Agriculture harvest estimate last week which put 1996 wheat supplies significantly higher at 18.9 million tonnes.
"The market is compounded by buying interest from the east for milling wheat. There is basic interest so prices are not in a downtrend," said one German grain trader.
Domestic millers were not covered and were likely to stay in the market while French arrivals did not compete fully. Another booster was lack of farm selling.
But the Hamburg grain exchange lowered its new crop bread wheat price (12.5 percent protein) by 2.50 marks this week to 285 marks and feed wheat by five marks to 270.
Barley stood higher but was illiquid.
French prices slipped with wheat into Rouen for Oct-Dec quoted at 875 francs, down from 890-895 francs last week. Barley for the same delivery fetched 860 francs, down 20 francs.
UK prices were ticking down on increased farm selling and strong sterling but recovered slightly on Wednesday.
Business was quiet in Spain with few fresh factors, although farmers had some transport problems as the sugar beet harvest placed trucks in short supply.

The first maize came in on the market in the northern region of Catalonia at 27,000 pesetas, although the harvest was not expected to start in earnest until October 20 when prices should feel some pressure, dealers said.
Italian durum and soft wheat were stable to slightly lower as demand was persistently weak.
"Demand for soft wheat from feed producers is starting to pick up slightly, but the amounts that have been asked are limited," said the Italian Istitute for Agricultural Studies (Ismea).
Maize traded lower despite the rains in northern Italy.
"Maize prices could stay at these levels for the rest of October," one dealer said.
